summary.prose: Story s7 makes signoff a real step in a team repo: the claim holder submits approved, reviewed artifacts as one request in the tracker, and the next stage will not start until the tracker reports that request completed. One read-only decision, taken by the stage an attempt follows, is used both by the team gate's completion hook and by an awaited step at the daemon's stage-start entries, which also records the tracker's answer on every artifact of the request together and releases the claim; the same step runs on demand through a team settle command, which is how a BUILD's request, held on the Story's issue, is read. Story and Epic completion wait inside the completion walk for signoff when the policy lists a member stage, so a listed artifact stays approved until it can be submitted, and signoff facts live in each artifact's lifecycle and are shown apart from model review and local approval.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: A daemon-side team gate over a synchronous, capability-declaring tracker port (alternative a1). The port (sc1) is the only way the workflow library talks to a tracker; GitHub is its first adapter, made by extracting the existing GitHub code (src/workflow/tracker, the issue calls in tracker-auto.ts, and the create and close calls in src/workflow/bugfix/tracker.ts) behind it. sc1 is the one tracker abstraction: the unbuilt tracker-tool design (LLD-38436e90625a83a2-s1) is not built as a second abstraction and is superseded or amended by s1's LLD. The policy (sc2) is read from the remote default branch and says which stages need signoff, whether claims are enforced, the claim units and the administrators. The artifact's tracker record keeps every existing meta.tracker field exactly as it is and gains additive per-unit data, plus an optional meta.revision (sc3). The team gate (sc4) takes a guarded action and returns an outcome. Signoff is a separate record (sc5) that never changes meta.review or approvedAt. Syncing tracker status on git pull and push, and the issue-status read it needs, are deferred with the later-tracker work to a define extend and are not part of this HLD.

ownedContracts.name: SignoffRecord
ownedContracts.purpose: A record separate from meta.review and approvedAt, stating that a signoff request completed and which artifacts and revisions it covered. The revision is the binding; a content hash is later hardening. Owned by s7.

consumedContracts.name: TrackerPort and PortResult
consumedContracts.purpose: The only way the workflow library talks to a tracker. Declares capabilities, is checked against the capabilities the policy needs when loaded, returns structured results with a distinct error for a missing tool or sign-in, and can say who the signed-in user is so the gate knows who is acting. An issue reference is the existing owner/repo#N string. Owned by s1 because s1 is a root and every consumer depends on it.

consumedContracts.name: TeamPolicy
consumedContracts.purpose: The central rules read from the remote default branch: team mode, signoff stages, claim enforcement, claim units, administrators, and the grandfathering anchor. Owned by s2.

consumedContracts.name: Per-unit tracker record and revision
consumedContracts.purpose: Adds data next to the artifact's existing meta.tracker without changing any existing field: a per-stage-unit issue map in a new key, and an optional meta.revision (default 0 when absent), minted on content writes and not on meta-only writes. A review that applies auto-fixes, whether through verdicts.ts or run-artifact.ts, is a content write; a report-only review is meta-only. Owned by s4, which also owns the inventory of artifact write paths and the shared issue-creation code.

consumedContracts.name: Team gate, claim state, gate outcome, refusal error and completion hook
consumedContracts.purpose: The single gate for guarded actions in the daemon-owned workflow library, the claim state read live from the tracker, the outcome type, the typed refusal error that leaves approval, the review-fix decision that both review paths (verdicts.ts and run-artifact.ts) consult, and a completion hook that s5 ships unregistered and s7 registers. The gate derives the acting user itself through the port, so no caller signature changes. Owned by s5; s4 supplies issue creation which the gate calls for the no-issue outcome.

boundary.internal: Opening the signoff request with the chosen artifacts, prerequisite checks for model review and local approval, registering the completion hook to produce the awaiting-signoff outcome, the on-demand completion check, automatic release of the claim on completion, recording sign-off together, grandfathering of artifacts approved before the policy anchor, and the separate display of signoff.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The GitHub adapter built by extracting src/workflow/tracker (including the existing signed-in-user read, ghCurrentLogin, behind whoAmI), the issue calls in tracker-auto.ts and the create and close calls in src/workflow/bugfix/tracker.ts behind the port; the gh command wrapper with its 10-second timeout; contract tests; detection of a missing tool or sign-in. The port receives the needed capabilities as an argument, so s1 does not read the policy. Reconciliation: the unbuilt tracker-tool design LLD-38436e90625a83a2-s1 (docs/standalone/add-add-items-tracker-setting-have-E2026100638436e90/S001/LLD.md) is not built as a second abstraction; sc1 is the one tracker abstraction and s1's LLD supersedes or amends that LLD, once its conflicting approval status is settled. Syncing tracker status on git pull and push, and an issue-status read on the port, are deferred to the define extend.

Reading the policy file from the remote default branch ref, the cached last-fetched copy and the offline rule, finding the first default-branch commit that carried the policy file, the starter policy and the team setup command.

The repo-scoped kind of row in the shared settings catalog whose reads and writes go to the per-repo map in github.json read by resolveGithubConfig; its rendering in VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal client; read-only display of policy values. Shares the single store with s1's target resolution.

Shared issue-creation code refactored out of autoPushEpicOnHld, autoPushStoryOnLld and autoPushTasksOnPlan, find-by-label dedupe for Story and Task issues, forcing Task issues on in team mode, daemon-side triggering when a draft is first written, the terminal approve path kept as manual fallback, the inventory and classification of artifact write paths (including the two writeFileSync writers, and both verdicts.ts and run-artifact.ts as content writes when auto-fixes change the body), the single content-write helper and the revision minting, the bypass test that also detects raw writeFileSync on artifact paths, and the rule that an artifact without meta.revision reads as revision 0.

The team gate and its call sites (daemon step entry points and approveArtifactByJsonPath), the acting-user read through the port, claim and release commands, live assignee reads, the guarded-action list (code-review and analyze are never guarded; review is never refused), the report-only review for a non-holder through the review-fix decision on both review paths (verdicts.ts and run-artifact.ts), the typed TeamGateRefusedError, its handling beside ReviewBlockedError in approveWorkflowTarget and its formatting in the terminal client's approve case in src/cli/command.ts, the no-issue outcome handling, administrator release, and the declaration of the completion hook, shipped unregistered.
Parking a draft on a handoff branch, the issue note, resuming from committed files, and reconstructing in-flight workflow state from committed artifacts instead of the opaque token.
Revision of an open request: re-run of local approval, push to the same request, discarding an earlier completion, refusing non-holders.
Private implementation of s9: Keep tracker issues and status in step with the work without a manual step

nonFunctional.performance: Each guarded action makes at most two live reads through the port (the signed-in user and the assignee); every tracker command has a 10-second timeout, after which the action is refused with the reason. A repo without a policy makes no tracker call.
nonFunctional.security: Policy is read only from the remote default branch ref and is not locally overridable; enforcement lives in the daemon-owned workflow library (k1); no tracker secrets are stored by insrc, sign-in stays with the tracker's CLI; administrators come only from the policy.
nonFunctional.observability: Every gate outcome other than allowed is logged with unit, action and reason; port failures carry their kind (missing-tool, missing-signin, unreachable, rejected).
nonFunctional.durability: Claim, issue and signoff state live in the tracker and in committed artifact files; the in-memory step state stores (100 entries, 1 hour) are not relied on for handoff. Artifact writes stay atomic through the existing helper.

dataModelChanges.details: sc5 record { request, artifacts: [{artifactId, revision}], completedAt, grandfathered? } produced by signoffRecordsOf from Lifecycle.signoffs; no stored stamp. The request Reference stored on each Signoff is { entityId: the request ref, type: 'signoff-request', relation: 'tracked-by' }, an existing member of the closed relation union, so the Reference type is not changed; the ref is read back from entityId, so settle and signoffRecordsOf group artifacts by it.

Gains the stage unit, the artifacts with revision and committed path, the branch and the issue to link from; SignoffRequestRef gains an optional url (the pending sc1 amendment AMD-315d510cb28100e2-16).

CAPABILITIES gains signoff-request, because loadTracker rejects a needed capability the adapter does not declare. Invariant at risk: the adapter declares only what it implements, so it is added together with the two methods and only then.
Gains trailing action and authoring arguments (sc4 amendment AMD-315d510cb28100e2-17); consultHook passes them. Invariant at risk: a hook written with three arguments keeps working.
Gains an optional holds predicate, (unitId) => boolean, that the completion walk consults for every unit it visits and that stops the walk at a unit it holds. Absent, the walk is unchanged.

completeThroughService passes signoffHoldsCompletion as the holds predicate, so the walk skips a held Story and therefore also the Epic above it, and settleSignoff runs the walk again once nothing is held. Invariant at risk: a Story completes, and cascades complete onto its members, as soon as its roll-up holds; with no policy, outside team mode, with no member stage listed, or with every listed member signed off or grandfathered the predicate is false and completion is unchanged.
Gains a signoff entry from signoffViewOf next to approval and review, which keep their values.
Gains the same signoff entry beside approval, review and reviewCurrency; the evidence of a story already includes its BUILD records, so a held BUILD shows its signoff state there.

Each existing artifact line (define, HLD and LLD) gains its signoff state after the approval state; no BUILD or Story-completion line is added, because the report carries none and a held BUILD is shown in the delivery evidence.
handoffRpcHandlers gains team.settle beside team.park and team.resume, and the terminal's team service gains teamSettle beside teamPark and teamResume.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: SignoffRecord is implemented as the HLD sketch, derived from lifecycle facts through signoffRecordsOf.

Uses openSignoffRequest, readSignoffState, readAssignee, whoAmI and setAssignee; the adapter declares signoff-request and implements the two signoff methods, and the request types are extended by the pending amendment.

Reads signoffStages, source.firstCommitTime and source.anchorKnown; claimUnits is read only for who may author, never to decide which unit a request belongs to; never grandfathers when anchorKnown is false.
Reads the unit issue and the revision the signoff is bound to.
Registers the completion hook in the daemon and the terminal, returns awaiting-signoff, and relies on the additive action and authoring arguments of AMD-315d510cb28100e2-17.

errorCases.scenario: An artifact is submitted without local approval at its current revision
errorCases.detection: openSignoff reads each artifact's lifecycle through approvalStateOf and compares the revision of the approval with the head revision
errorCases.response: Refuse before any tracker call, naming the artifact and that local approval is missing
errorCases.userImpact: The holder sees which artifact needs approval and approves it first

errorCases.scenario: A DEF, HLD or LLD is submitted without an other-party review
errorCases.detection: openSignoff reads lifecycleReviewOf for the head and checks the review exists and its reviewer is not the author
errorCases.response: Refuse before any tracker call, naming the artifact and the missing review
errorCases.userImpact: The holder runs the review first

errorCases.scenario: A BUILD is submitted without a usable code review
errorCases.detection: openSignoff reads the Story's code-review CR record and checks it exists, was written by the other party and its body.verdict is not block, because a BUILD head carries no lifecycle review
errorCases.response: Refuse before any tracker call, saying the code review is missing, written by the author, or blocking
errorCases.userImpact: The holder completes or resolves the code review first

errorCases.scenario: The submitter is not the holder, or nobody holds the unit
errorCases.detection: openSignoff reads the assignee of the issue of the unit that holds the stage (the epic for DEF and HLD, the story for LLD and BUILD) through port.readAssignee and compares it with port.whoAmI, because teamGate returns allowed for open-signoff on an unassigned stage
errorCases.response: Refuse with a TeamGateRefusedError naming the holder, or saying the stage must be claimed first when nobody holds it; no request is opened
errorCases.userImpact: A non-holder is told who holds the unit; on an unassigned stage the user claims it before submitting, and for a BUILD it is the Story's issue that must be claimed

errorCases.scenario: The stage is not listed in signoffStages
errorCases.detection: openSignoff finds the artifacts' stage absent from policy.signoffStages
errorCases.response: Refuse saying the policy does not ask for signoff at this stage
errorCases.userImpact: The author continues with local approval alone

errorCases.scenario: The artifact to submit is no longer approved because its Story or Epic completed first
errorCases.detection: openSignoff reads the head's status as completed and open-signoff would be an illegal transition from it
errorCases.response: Refuse naming the status; this cannot arise for a listed, non-grandfathered stage in team mode because the holds predicate keeps the completion walk from completing it, so it signals an artifact that completed before the policy listed its stage
errorCases.userImpact: The holder is told the artifact is already completed and cannot be submitted

errorCases.scenario: The tracker cannot be loaded because the adapter lacks signoff-request
errorCases.detection: loadTracker returns a not-ok PortResult naming the missing capability
errorCases.response: Return the refusal with its reason; there is no degraded mode
errorCases.userImpact: Signoff is unavailable for that tracker until it declares the capability

errorCases.scenario: The tracker cannot open the request (missing tool, missing sign-in, unreachable, rejected)
errorCases.detection: openSignoffRequest returns a not-ok PortResult with its kind
errorCases.response: Return the PortResult with its reason; record nothing on any artifact
errorCases.userImpact: The holder sees the cause and retries

errorCases.scenario: Recording open-signoff fails part-way across the artifacts of a request
errorCases.detection: LifecycleService.apply rejects for one artifact after others were recorded
errorCases.response: Stop and report; a repeat finds the open request through the Reference already stored on the recorded artifacts and records only the rest, never opening a second request

errorCases.scenario: The stored request Reference cannot be read back as a request ref
errorCases.detection: settleSignoff or signoffRecordsOf finds a Signoff whose Reference type is not signoff-request or whose entityId is empty
errorCases.response: Skip that Signoff, log it, and keep the stage blocked
errorCases.userImpact: The next stage stays refused and the log names the artifact

errorCases.scenario: The tracker cannot be read during settle
errorCases.response: settleSignoff records nothing for that request and logs the kind; settleForAttempt then throws the awaiting-signoff refusal because blockedBySignoff still blocks; team.settle reports the failure
errorCases.userImpact: The next stage is refused, or the settle command says the tracker could not be read, until it is reachable

errorCases.scenario: Settle fails part-way recording signed-off across a completed request
errorCases.detection: LifecycleService.apply rejects for one artifact after others were recorded
errorCases.response: Stop; blockedBySignoff refuses while any artifact of a completed request is unrecorded; the next settle records the rest; the claim is released and the deferred completion runs only after all are recorded
errorCases.userImpact: The next stage waits for the next attempt, and no artifact stays signed off alone

errorCases.response: Settle applies signoff-changes to every artifact of the request; the attempt is refused saying changes were requested and linking the request
errorCases.userImpact: The holder revises through s8's flow

errorCases.scenario: Clearing the assignee on completion fails
errorCases.detection: setAssignee returns a not-ok PortResult after all artifacts were recorded
errorCases.response: Log it and continue; the artifacts stay signed off and the next stage proceeds
errorCases.userImpact: The claim stays until released by the holder or an administrator

errorCases.scenario: The deferred Story or Epic completion fails after signoff was recorded
errorCases.detection: completeIfRolledUp throws or returns no completed ids while the holds predicate is now false and the roll-up holds
errorCases.response: Log it and leave the signoff recorded; the completion is retried by the next settle, by team.settle and by the next approval of a BUILD
errorCases.userImpact: The Story stays approved until the next attempt completes it

errorCases.scenario: A BUILD's request completes but no stage start follows
errorCases.detection: nothing reads a request that follows no stage, so the held Story stays approved; the user sees the BUILD record in the delivery evidence with its signoff entry still open (DeliveryEvidenceEntry lists a story's BUILD records), since the chain report has no BUILD line
errorCases.response: The user runs team settle for the Story, which makes the daemon read the request, record signed-off on the BUILD and run the held completion
errorCases.userImpact: The Story completes once team settle runs after the tracker reports completion

errorCases.scenario: A first author turn is attempted on a story whose issue could not be created while the HLD awaits signoff
errorCases.detection: teamGate returns allowFirstAuthor before it consults the hook, so settleForAttempt calls blockedBySignoff itself at the entry before the gate is reached
errorCases.response: Refuse with the awaiting-signoff outcome at the entry; the gate's exception is not reached
errorCases.userImpact: The first turn is refused until the HLD is signed off

errorCases.scenario: The hook runs in a process where it was not registered
errorCases.detection: A test asserts both entry points call registerSignoffHook
errorCases.response: Registration is added at the daemon start and in makeServices in the terminal; a missing registration fails that test, and the entry step still refuses in the daemon

edgeCases.input: A repo without a policy file, teamMode off or claims not enforced
edgeCases.expected: The hook, settle and the holds predicate make no tracker call and change nothing; the next stage and completion proceed as today

edgeCases.input: A policy listing LLD or BUILD when the BUILD of the Story's last task is approved
edgeCases.expected: The approval stands, the walk stops at the held Story and so does not reach the Epic, and the BUILD and LLD stay approved until their signoff is recorded

edgeCases.expected: The request still belongs to the Story's issue, because the BUILD record is Story-scoped; claimUnits decides who may author a task's build, not which unit holds a request

edgeCases.input: A Story whose every listed member is signed off while its Epic's DEF or HLD is listed and unsigned
edgeCases.expected: The Story completes, the walk then stops at the held Epic, and the Epic completes when its listed members are signed off or grandfathered

edgeCases.input: A policy listing neither LLD nor BUILD nor DEF nor HLD
edgeCases.expected: The holds predicate is false and the Story and Epic complete as soon as their roll-up holds

edgeCases.input: A pre-anchor LLD that stays approved and is never submitted, with anchorKnown true

edgeCases.input: The same artifact when anchorKnown is false
edgeCases.expected: Nothing is grandfathered: it blocks the next stage and holds completion until it is signed off

edgeCases.input: Authoring design.story on a story unit while the HLD on the epic has an open request
edgeCases.expected: The attempt is judged by the HLD on the epic unit and refused as awaiting signoff; the same unit's LLD request does not block its own authoring

edgeCases.input: Authoring plan on the same story unit while the LLD has an open request
edgeCases.expected: The attempt is judged by the LLD on the story and refused as awaiting signoff

edgeCases.input: A planned task build while the Story's LLD is signed off
edgeCases.expected: The attempt follows the LLD on the story and proceeds

edgeCases.input: An attempt that follows BUILD, or any other action
edgeCases.expected: followedStageOf returns null and nothing blocks

edgeCases.input: The next stage is attempted after the artifact was edited since it was signed off
edgeCases.expected: Editing returned the head to draft, so approval and signoff are needed again; the old signoff covers the older revision

edgeCases.input: A request holds several artifacts and the tracker reports completed
edgeCases.expected: Every artifact is recorded signed-off together, none alone

edgeCases.input: A pending request exists while the attempted action is open-signoff, revise or release
edgeCases.expected: The hook returns continue so submission and retry never meet their own refusal

edgeCases.input: A later phase of a run already started (plan, step, synthesize, validate)
edgeCases.expected: Only the registered hook judges it, from the recorded state, with no tracker call

edgeCases.input: Two clones settle the same completed request
edgeCases.expected: The second finds the artifacts already signed off and does nothing

invariantsToPreserve.text: The meaning of meta.review and of local approval does not change; signoff is never counted as a review and is shown beside them.
A repo without the policy file, with teamMode off or with claims not enforced behaves exactly as today, with no tracker call.
A BUILD's review stays the code-review record and never the lifecycle review.

A Story completes and cascades complete onto its members, and the walk continues to its Epic, as soon as the roll-up holds, unless the policy lists a member stage that is neither signed off nor grandfathered.
The Reference type's relation stays the closed union it is today.

alternativesConsidered.name: Read-only decision, an async settle step at the entries and on demand, a completion hold inside the walk, lifecycle facts, pull request as the request
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: One read-only check (blockedBySignoff) judges an attempt by the stage it follows and is used by the sync hook and by the async settle entry step; settle also runs on demand through team.settle, which is how a BUILD's request is read; Story and Epic completion are held inside the completion walk until every listed, non-grandfathered member is signed off; signoff facts live in Lifecycle.signoffs.

alternativesConsidered.name: Make the gate and the hook asynchronous
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: teamGate, assertMayAuthor and the hook return promises so the hook can record signoff itself.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Meets most criteria but breaks sc4's synchronous contract across about a dozen call sites and leaves the first-author gap open; a larger blast radius than a1.

alternativesConsidered.name: A stored meta.signoffs stamp and a synchronous write in the hook
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Write SignoffRecord into each artifact's meta synchronously from the hook, as the HLD sketches it.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Duplicates Lifecycle.signoffs, drifts from the common model and violates the read-only nature of the gate (sc4).
